title: OpenAI's chief scientist calls the lab's AI "an alien mind" - TCR 09/07/26
description:
OpenAI reported its coding agents now log 3.1 workdays of effort for every human workday inside its research org as chief scientist Jakub Pachocki called the systems an alien mind, independent evaluators RoboCurve and EEBench tested GPT-6 Astra's robot-arm and circuit-design claims where it placed a block 19 of 20 times but solved a precision puzzle only twice, and Edinburgh delivery riders began reverse-engineering the Deliveroo pay algorithm after fees fell from £3.67 to £3.42 per order.

https://sharedsapience.com/the-century-report-september-7-2026/

0:00 Open and framing
1:03 OpenAI's agents accelerate its own research
4:18 Independent tests probe GPT-6 Astra
6:47 Delivery riders rebuild the pay algorithm
9:32 Authors defend their settlement share
12:25 AIMe names the unknown molecules
15:11 Close

This episode covers OpenAI's research-acceleration data and Pachocki's alien-mind essay, the RoboCurve and EEBench independent tests of GPT-6 Astra, Edinburgh riders and the Workers' Observatory rebuilding the pay algorithm, the 2026 tech layoff numbers reframed against corporate filings, the AIMe neuro-symbolic system naming the dark matter of human metabolism, and authors defending their share of Anthropic's $1.5 billion settlement.

OpenAI's own report shows agent runtime now exceeding human labor time across its research organization, with total agent runtime passing human labor time, on OpenAI's measure, sometime after May and the 90th-percentile research user using more than $7,000 worth of tokens a day. Over half of the successful four-to-eight-hour tasks still needed a human to step in, so the work is relocating toward choosing which questions are worth the compute and judging what comes back. Chief scientist Jakub Pachocki calls what he works with an alien mind, intelligence grown more than designed, and asks for independent verification and public tracking of the pace. Two outside groups, RoboCurve and EEBench, put GPT-6 Astra's robot-arm and circuit-design demos to the test, and the checking is being assembled by parties the vendor does not control. Edinburgh delivery riders are rebuilding the algorithm that sets their pay from their own logs, a separate accounting reframes 2026's biggest layoff numbers against corporate filings, the AIMe system names the dark matter of human metabolism, and Anthropic's $1.5 billion settlement entered claim reconciliation through a public docket.
